Summary
Data source overview: The paper analyzes why modern image-classification networks are brittle to adversarial examples and proposes two complementary defenses: (1) a Defense Learning Network (DLN) that sanitises inputs before they reach the classifier and (2) a Noise Augmented Classifier (NAC) that adds small random noise to the logits. The authors also show how repeated DLN training and the combination DLN+NAC further increase robustness.

Extraction confidence[87]
Inference strategy justification: All nodes are direct paraphrases of explicit claims, mechanisms, methods or interventions described in Sections 1–5. Moderate inference (confidence 2) was only used to link repeated DLN and combined defence to the underlying risk because the paper states qualitative rather than formal causal links.
Extraction completeness: 15 concept nodes and 4 intervention nodes capture every distinct element in the causal chain from the risk of adversarial misclassification to each actionable defence proposed, with all reasoning steps preserved and interconnected.
Key limitations: 1) The paper contains detailed mathematical derivations that were abstracted into single “definition/metric” nodes. 2) Empirical evidence strength was judged qualitatively because exact p-values are not provided.
